text: {"final": {"summary": "P1: wrote scripts/disburse_cycle2.py following the ops-script conventions (repo root on sys.path, docstring declaring it appends to data/outbox/payments.jsonl and data/outbox/sms.jsonl). It loads active households via registry.register.load_households(active_only=True), decides eligibility with eligibility.rules.is_eligible (no score recomputation), and for each eligible household calls payments.vouchers.disburse(h.id, 60, payments.vouchers.payment_key(h.id, 2)) — no manual Payment/ID construction, no explicit now (records timestamped by config.settings.now(), 2026-03-10T08:00:00). After a successful disbursement it queues notifications.sms.queue_sms(h.id, 'PAYMENT_SENT', {'amount': 60, 'cycle': 2, 'ref': payment.id}). DuplicatePayment is caught and the household is skipped, making re-runs idempotent. It prints the paid household IDs, payments.receipts.total_paid(), and per-household receipts_for(h.id) counts for verification. P2: ran the script once. Verification from its output and the outbox: all 16 currently eligible households (HH-10170, HH-10332, HH-10421, HH-10650, HH-11169, HH-12858, HH-13498, HH-13919, HH-14060, HH-14133, HH-14419, HH-14923, HH-15407, HH-16705, HH-16723, HH-16888) each have exactly one cycle-2 payment of 60 dollars (keys HH-xxxx:2, PAY-00016..PAY-00031, sent_at 2026-03-10T08:00:00); the run reported them as already-paid duplicates (idempotent skip), so nothing was paid twice and no new payments were needed. No ineligible household appears in the payments outbox; total_paid is 1860 (900 from cycle 1 + 960 from the 16 cycle-2 payments).", "done_steps": ["P1", "P2"]}}
